text:
## Settling "sandbox" versus "3 maps x 3 variations"

| Question | Official answer | Source |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| What does "sandbox" mean? | Player-driven play space with build and destroy freedom; "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox"; clips recorded in a "100 player Tactical All Out Warfare sandbox" | [1][4][5] |
| Is there an open-world sandbox map? | No official text says so. The mode is a King of the Hill style fight over a Control Zone "within larger maps" | [1][2] |
| How many maps? | Three maps with three variations each (Team17 press release, quoted via the foundation; not re-read here) | [9] |
| What is a "variation"? | Not defined in any official text read | [1][2][3] |

Assessment: Medium confidence that "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations" are compatible. "Sandbox" describes freedom of play inside a map; the press release counts map assets. The official 18 Feb post describes "multiple locations and POIs" in the setting "Kolchia" [2], which could be what a "variation" refers to, but this is an inference and unconfirmed.

## Map scale: what official text says

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Control Zone size: randomised 2x2 km | Steam page, Season 01 (checked 2026-10-08); also 18 Feb 2026 post | [1][2] |
| Map size: 256 km² | 18 Feb 2026 post (pre-release); not repeated on the Steam page | [2] |
| Max players per match: 100 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Teams: 3 | Season 01 | [1][2] |
| Points to win: 100 | Season 01 | [1][2] |

Assessment: Medium confidence that 256 km² remains current. It is official but dated seven months before launch, and the Steam page uses only "larger maps". The 2x2 km zone is 4 km², about 1.6% of 256 km² (arithmetic from [2]). Community figures (about 16 km edge to edge, 500 m radius play circles) are player-reported or unattributed, and the 500 m figure conflicts with the 2x2 km zone [12][13].

## Level design philosophy as stated

Official statements are thin. The 16 Jul 2026 devlog gives three points: real-world reference gathering in Georgia, continuous optimisation across a wide range of hardware, and tunable graphics options [3]. The 21 May 2026 Debrief lists "real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" and "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox" [5]. The Top Questions post says the setting offers "varied, grounded militaristic gameplay" with "multiple locations and POIs" [2]. No official text describes sightline, chokepoint or zone-placement design rules. Playtesters are quoted as surprised at performance, which is Bulkhead's own characterisation [3].

## What can be destroyed

| Item | Status | Source |
|------|--------|--------|
| Apartment blocks | Destroyable by rocket launchers | [1] |
| Towns and buildings generally | "Destructible battlefield"; tanks can "tear your way through towns" | [1] |
| Player buildables (FOB parts, schematics) | Destroyable; destruction reward scales with build progress since 0.1.2 | [7] |
| Terrain deformation | No official statement; a third-party roadmap claims terrain is destructible | [12] |
| Persistence across matches | No official statement | - |
| Which structures are indestructible | No official list | - |

Destruction is also a listed Early Access pillar: "Destruction & Build Mechanics" [2], and "Infantry, Vehicles, Base Building & Destruction" in the announcement trailer post [4]. The roles list includes Demolitions [4]. The gameplay trailer post lists "building, destruction" among the features [6]. Player-built structure rules are in fob-and-base-building.

## Destruction and performance

No official source ties destruction to a performance cost, a debris cap or a server tick budget. What is official: Bulkhead built a custom framework on UE5 to handle 100 players [2]; performance was prioritised from day one [3]; graphics options exist [3]. The Steam requirements and minimum spec are in system-requirements-and-performance. Assessment: Low confidence that destruction limits exist; the KB neither confirms nor denies them.

## Weather and rain (Season 02)

The official Season 02 teaser gives only the date, 15 Oct 2026 [8]. The 0.1.2 notes say Season 02 brings "new map conditions" [7]. Press reports that rain is an extra per-map weather state, not a dynamic mid-match event, quoting Bulkhead [10][11]. The Bulkhead text itself was not available in the saved official posts, so rain remains press-reported (confidence Medium). Whether rain affects visibility, vehicles or aircraft is unconfirmed [11].

| Maps 3, variations 3 each | Season 01 launch, press release | [9] |
| Minimum spec: GTX 1660 / RX 590, 16 GB RAM, 50 GB, 1080p Low 60 fps (upscaled) | Steam page, 2026-10-08 | [1] |
| Recommended spec: RTX 3070 / RX 6700 XT, 1440p Medium 70+ fps native or 4K Medium 60+ upscaled | Steam page, 2026-10-08 | [1] |
| Starting cash $10,000 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Buildable destruction reward scales with build progress | Patch 0.1.2, 30 Sep 2026 | [7] |
| Weather states at baseline: none documented; rain announced | Pre-Season-02 | [8][10] |

text:
Officially, WARDOGS launched with three maps, each with three variations, and a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside a larger battlefield [1][2]. No official source names the maps, profiles them, or explains how they rotate. This reference collects the per-map profiles that exist, all of which are player-reported: Bakurani, Ozeti and Zestafona, plus the unconfirmed Jutari and Saburtulo [3][4][5][6][7].

Several community sources agree on the three names, their settings and the existence of roughly three rotating areas per map. They disagree on play-area size, control-zone counts and whether a fourth map exists. Rain is the only announced Season 02 environment change [8].

Confidence is Low: the core claims are player-reported and the sources conflict. Nothing here adds official evidence to the foundation document.

- Official: three maps with three variations each; "large-scale maps with dynamic objective zones"; Eastern European derelict industrial mountains; Control Zones are randomised 2x2 km areas within larger maps (Sep 2026) [1][2].
- Official sources do not name any map or give a map size [1][2].
- Player-reported: the three playable maps are Bakurani, Ozeti and Zestafona [3][4][5][7].
- Player-reported: allthings.how lists Bakurani Outskirts (Jutari) and Saburtulo as not confirmed playable; its introduction mentions "four playable battlegrounds" while its detailed sections list three [3].
- Press quote of Bulkhead: Season 02 rain is "an additional weather state per map and not a dynamic event mid match"; Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 [8].
title: Launch Maps Reference
topic: Per-map profiles: Bakurani, Ozeti, Zestafona and unconfirmed maps

text:
## Map profiles (all player-reported, Season 01)

| Attribute | Bakurani | Ozeti | Zestafona |
|-----------|----------|-------|-----------|
| Region label | Kavkazi [3] | Europe [3] | North America [3] |
| Setting | Eastern European mountain river valley [3][4][7] | Wooded river basin around a hill town [3][4][5] | Industrial rail hub on a river bend [4][5][7] |
| Relative size | Smallest [4] | About 4x Bakurani's play area [4] | About 4x Bakurani's play area [4] |
| Play-circle radius (community) | 500 m [3] | 550 m [3] | 500 m [3] |
| Terrain | Valley floor, factory district, forested ridges, farmland, snowy northern peaks [3][4] | Hill town, orchards, farmland, forest, river across the south [3][4] | Warehouses, rail yards, shipping, farmland, forest [3][4] |
| Named areas | Default, Farmland, Lumberyard [3][7] | Default, Church, River (Farmland defined but not in rotation) [3][7] | Default, Water Treatment, Houses (Small Factory defined but not in rotation) [3][6][7] |

## Notable points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Features | Source |
|-----|----------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, factory and containers, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, sunflower fields and church, Lumberyard, numbered towers (7 plus 4 abandoned in one list; 5 drill towers in another) | [4][7] |
| Ozeti | Walled football stadium with parking and garages, six-part Hillside Church, Apartments, Shops, Pool, Industrial, farms, 4 towers in two lists | [3][4][7] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, offices, water towers, northern Water Treatment, 3 drill towers | [4][6][7] |

## Typical Control Zone behaviour (player-reported)

- allthings.how: one objective ring of 85 m radius at the centre of the live play area; on Zestafona the three live areas are picked at equal frequency [3][6]. On Bakurani it says the Default area is picked twice as often as the other two [3]; no other source says this.
- allthings.how: the farthest area centres are 285 m apart on Bakurani, 693 m on Ozeti and 531 m on Zestafona [3][6]. These distances fit a 500 m circle model, not a 2x2 km zone.
- Hot Zone: roams inside the Control Zone and counts double [6][7]. Boostroom says Bulkhead confirms double cash for it; I could not trace that to an official page [7].
- Terrain effect: Bakurani high ground over the valley road decides engagements [3]; Ozeti open approaches to the town are exposed [3][7]; Zestafona has long exposed approaches in the yards [3][7].

## Unconfirmed maps

| Map | Claim | Source |
|-----|-------|--------|
| Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari | Sniper Showdown map on the Kavkazi world; 350 m play circle, 75 m objective ring, single fixed area, no rotation; status "not confirmed as playable" | [3] |
| Saburtulo | Listed as a King of the Hill map under Russia; no play area or objective; not playable | [3] |

No other source read mentions either name; the guides from xgamingserver.com, gamebrief.net and boostroom.com name only three maps [4][5][7]. Treat both as unconfirmed.

## Rotation

- Official: no rotation is documented. Bulkhead says only that the Control Zone is randomised [1].
- Player-reported: each map has three live areas drawn from a defined list of three or four; allthings.how says selection on Zestafona is equally likely [3][6]. Gamebrief says the whole map is not confirmed to reroll each match and no map vote or map order is documented [5].
- Assessment (Low): the "three variations" per map [2] plausibly match the three live areas, but no source states this.

## Conflicts between sources

| Topic | Source A | Source B | Treatment |
|-------|----------|----------|-----------|
| Play area | Official 2x2 km Control Zone [1] | 500 m radius circles, 85 m ring [3][6] | Not reconciled; official figure stands, community figures unverified |
| Whole-map size | Boostroom: 256 km2 attributed to Bulkhead [7] | Steam page gives no map size [1] | Attribution not verifiable |
| Control zones | 171 named zones across three maps [4] | One ring per map [3]; three to four positions per map [5] | No figure adopted |
| Map count | Three maps [2][4][5] | allthings.how introduction says four playable, details list three [3] | Three; internal inconsistency noted |
| Tower count | Bakurani 7 plus 4 abandoned [4] | Bakurani 5 drill towers [7] | Not reconciled |
| Bakurani rotation | Default picked twice as often [3] | No weighting documented [5][7] | Single source |

## Season 02 weather

Rain is announced as one extra weather state per map, set for the whole match; it does not change mid match, and the effect on visibility or gameplay was not stated [8]. The coverage mentions no new map [8]. Nothing else about the Season 02 environment is taken as fact here.

text:
Officially, WARDOGS launched in Early Access on 10 September 2026 with three maps, each with three variations, set in "derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe" on a destructible battlefield [1][2]. The Steam page does not name the maps, give a map size, or define "variations". Every match is played around a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside a larger battlefield [1].

The map names (Bakurani, Ozeti, Zestafona), their points of interest and the relative sizes come only from community-run references and are player-reported [9][10][11]. Bulkhead has announced rain as an extra weather state per map for Season 02 (15 Oct 2026), not a mid-match event [3][4]. No fourth map is announced [4][8].

Confidence is Low. The official sources give counts and a setting but no names or dimensions. The named detail rests on community directories that disagree with each other on play-area size.

text:
- Launch content is three maps, each with three variations (Team17 press release, 10 Sep 2026) [2].
- The Steam page calls the game a "militaristic sandbox" for up to 100 players, set on a destructible battlefield; rocket launchers can destroy apartment blocks [1]. "Sandbox" describes building and destruction freedom, not a separate map type (Assessment: Medium, see Detail) [1].
- Official sources do not name the maps. Community directories list Bakurani, Ozeti and Zestafona (player-reported, Season 01) [9][10][11].
- A third-party roadmap piece gives a 256 km2 destructible map; a community guide gives about 16 km edge to edge. These agree arithmetically but neither is official [7][11].
- The play area is the randomised 2x2 km Control Zone [1]; one community guide instead claims 500 m radius circles, a conflict left open [11].
- Season 02 (15 Oct 2026) adds rain as a per-map weather state, not a dynamic mid-match event [3][4]. No new map is announced [4][8].
- More maps are planned for 1.0, with no names or dates [1][7].

Verified 2026-10-08.

- The setting is "derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe"; the battlefield is destructible and includes towns and apartment blocks [1].
- Early Access maps are described as large-scale with dynamic objective zones [1].
- Players can destroy apartment blocks with rocket launchers and drive armoured vehicles through towns [1].
- Players can build and fortify key locations, for example a forward operating base at a chokepoint [1].
- The launch set is three maps, each with three variations [2].
- The only official size statement is that the Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area inside a larger battlefield; total map size is not stated on the Steam page [1].
- More maps are planned alongside weapons, vehicles and fighter jets; no map is named [1].
- Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 in Bulkhead's Steam teaser, and rain is "an additional weather state per map and not a dynamic event mid match" per a Bulkhead post quoted by press [3][4]. An unofficial wiki says the 30 Sep 2026 announcement mentions "new map conditions" without detail [8]; this is player-reported.
- The 0.1.2 notes and Season 1 changelog contain no new map, terrain or weather entries [5][6].

text:
## Reconciling "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations"

The Steam page says "sandbox" and "maps" with no count [1]. The press release gives the count: three maps with three variations each [2]. These are compatible: "sandbox" describes the build-and-destroy freedom, while the press release counts discrete map assets. Assessment: Medium confidence that this is the intended reading, because neither official source defines either term.

The word "variations" is not defined. A community guide lists about three or four named areas per map (for example Default, Farmland, Lumberyard on Bakurani) that come up from a rotation, with some defined areas never selected [11]. This plausibly matches the "three variations" count but is an inference; no source confirmed sunrise or cloudy variants of the maps. Treat the equivalence as unverified.

## Community-reported map roster (Season 01, player-reported)

| Map | Region label | Described terrain | Relative size | Source |
|-----|--------------|-------------------|---------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Kavkazi | River valley, town, factory district, snow-capped northern mountains | Smallest | [9][10][11] |
| Ozeti | Europe | Wooded river basin, hill town, walled football stadium, church, farmland | About 4x Bakurani | [9][10][11] |
| Zestafona | North America | River bend, warehouse and rail districts, shipping, farmland, forest | About 4x Bakurani | [9][10][11] |

A further "Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari" sniper map and "Saburtulo" appear in one roster but are listed as not confirmed playable or not playable [11]. They are not counted as launch maps.

## Points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Named features | Source |
|-----|----------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, Sunflower complex and church, Lumberyard, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, numbered towers | [10] |
| Ozeti | Stadium complex, hillside churches, Shops, Pool, Industrial, Lumberyard, farms, numbered towers | [10] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, large factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, Offices, Water Towers, farmland | [10] |

One guide counts 171 control zones across the three maps [10]. Another records three or four zone positions per map and three live tower objectives on Zestafona [9]. These counts differ, so no figure is given as fact.

## Size

| Claim | Value | Class | Source |
|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| Control Zone | Randomised 2x2 km inside a larger battlefield | Official | [1] |
| Whole map | 256 km2, fully destructible | Third-party roadmap | [7] |
| Whole world | About 16 km edge to edge | Community | [11] |
| Play circle | 500 m radius (550 m Ozeti) | Community | [11] |

Assessment: 16 km x 16 km equals 256 km2, so the two whole-map figures agree, but both are unofficial (Low confidence). The 500 m radius play-circle claim conflicts with the official 2x2 km zone and is not adopted [1][11].

## Destructibility

Official: a destructible battlefield where rocket launchers destroy apartment blocks [1]; the press release lists destruction as a core pillar alongside construction [2]. No source gives a per-structure destruction model, which terrain can be deformed, or whether damage persists across matches. A third-party piece says terrain as well as buildings can be reshaped [7]; the official sources only mention buildings.

## Weather and time of day

Rain is the only announced weather addition, shown in the Season 02 teaser as heavy rain and storm imagery [3][4][8]. Bulkhead says it is a per-map state fixed for the match [3]. One press piece reports it is unconfirmed whether rain affects visibility or vehicles [4]. No day/night cycle is documented in any source read; a claim of existing sunrise, cloudy and sunny states was seen only in a search summary and is not relied on.

title: Community Channels & Source Reliability Register
topic: Official channels, community hubs, and a reliability rating for every source class and outlet used

text:
This document does two jobs. First, it lists the channels BULKHEAD and Team17 are confirmed to use for WARDOGS, based on the official Steam posts saved locally on 2026-10-08. Second, it rates every outlet and site cited anywhere in this knowledge base for reliability, commercial conflict of interest and track record against the official text. It is the basis for future staleness and trust decisions.

The Steam store page and the Steam News hub are the only channels whose address and content are fully verified. Official posts confirm that a community Discord and "socials" exist [6][11], and that a Twitch show and a contest site were used [9][22], but the snapshots contain no Discord invite or X handle. On 2026-10-08 Steam showed 109,396 reviews (all languages), 74.3% positive, "Mostly Positive" [3].

Confidence is Medium. The channel and review facts rest on official or first-party data (High on their own). The outlet ratings are judgements. I did not re-open every outlet page this session, so track-record notes compare claims already recorded in other KB documents against the official posts, and each rating states that basis.

text:
- Steam is the authoritative channel: 32 of the 65 items in the saved news feed are official posts from BULKHEAD (Steam news snapshot, 2026-10-08) [1][2].
- Official posts confirm a community Discord of "10k+ members" on 9 Feb 2026 and refer to "socials" and Discord announcements, but give no invite link or X handle; those stay unconfirmed [6][7].
- Steam showed 81,290 positive and 28,106 negative reviews (109,396 total, all languages) at 2026-10-08, score label "Mostly Positive" [3].
- Steam post bodies are now readable from the local snapshot, so patch facts can rest on official text. The earlier "bodies do not render" caveat in other documents is resolved for the 32 official posts.
- Official text confirms, against earlier uncertainty: the 2 Oct balance hotfix (IR Rangefinders disabled until Season 02, CIWS about 6 s instead of 12 s) [21], the 30 Sep date for 0.1.2 [19], and three approved hosts named on 8 Sep [22].
- Official text does not support any Season 02 "progression wipe" claim. The teaser gives only a date (15 Oct 2026) and a trailer [17].
- Commercial sellers (boosting, hosting) and single-source outlets are rated lowest; their claims are leads, never facts (see the register).

- **Official**: authored by BULKHEAD or Team17 (Steam announcements, official sites, press release). Source rank 1-3 in `SOURCE_REGISTRY.md`.
- **Press**: independent news outlet reporting on the game (rank 5).
- **Player-reported**: fan sites, guides, wikis, hosts, sellers (ranks 4 and 6). Never establishes a fact alone.
- **COI**: commercial conflict of interest, meaning the publisher sells something the article promotes (boosting, hosting, cash).
- **Reliability grade**: R1 matches official text and is usable as a secondary confirmation; R2 usable with corroboration; R3 lead only, label player-reported; R4 do not cite for facts. Grades are Assessment, not fact.
- **Baseline**: values recorded before the Season 02 wipe window so later diffs are mechanical.

## Editions (checked 2026-10-08)

The Steam page lists WARDOGS, the Supporter Edition bundle ("includes WARDOGS and WARDOGS - Supporter Pack"), and the Supporter Pack as DLC [1]. The main page does not list the pack's contents; the DLC's own store entry does [1][2].

## Supporter Pack contents

The DLC entry says the pack "offers extra camos and cosmetic content" and lists three Starter Weapon camos, three branded weapon and vehicle camos, a scoreboard supporter icon and two bobbleheads [2]. The developer states there is no monetisation during Early Access beyond this optional pack, that in-game cash and gold bars must be earned through play, and that camos cannot be purchased directly [2]. The launch press release repeats that in-game cash, gold bars and status-based camouflage are not for sale [4]. Nothing in these sources lists a gameplay advantage, so the cosmetic-only claim is the developer's statement, not independently tested.

## Platforms

Steam lists Windows only (Windows 10 minimum, Windows 11 recommended) and the API reports no Mac or Linux support [1][2]. Xbox and PlayStation 5 versions are planned for "sometime in 2028"; Xbox Store wishlists were reported open on 10 Sep 2026 [5][6].

## Review snapshot

The Steam page showed "Mostly Positive", 79% of 63,179 English reviews, on 2026-10-08 (time of day not shown; the foundation recorded 63,152 earlier the same day) [1]. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026 [6].

## Early Access pricing statement

The Steam page: "we plan for WARDOGS to be priced lower during Early Access" and "we may raise the price closer to full release" [1]. The press release describes a tiered model rewarding earlier backers and gives USD 39.99 [4]. No full-release price or Early Access end date is published [4].

A developer comment dated 25 Sep 2026 (appearing in the reader comments of that article) says there is no new timeline and they will announce confirmed compatibility [7]. In August a developer said on the Steam forums they were working on Proton support [8]. No Steam Deck Verified rating was found [8]. Reports about which anti-cheat blocks Linux are unconfirmed [7].

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter developed by BULKHEAD (Derby, UK) and published by Team17 [1][2]. It entered Steam Early Access on 10 September 2026 at a Standard price of GBP 36.99 on the UK Steam page and USD 39.99 in the launch press release [1][2][7]. Console versions are planned for "sometime in 2028" [4][5]. The developers expect Early Access to last about one to two years, with a higher price at full release [1].

Since launch the game has had a launch-day Season 1.0 changelog (10 Sep), Patch 0.11 (14 Sep), Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep) and a security and stability hotfix (2 Oct) [8][9][10]. Season 02 is scheduled for 15 October 2026 but its contents are only partly known [11][12]. Steam shows a "Mostly Positive" review rating [1].

Confidence is Medium. Dates, platforms, price and the developer's roadmap text come from the Steam page and Team17, but patch contents rest on press summaries because Steam news bodies do not render to fetchers, and Season 02 detail comes from secondary or conflicted sources.

text:
## Developer, publisher and platforms

BULKHEAD is a Derby-based studio founded in 2015, previously known for The Turing Test and Battalion 1944; Team17 (part of everplay Group plc) publishes [2]. The Steam page lists BULKHEAD as developer and Team17 as publisher [1]. As of 2026-10-08 the playable platform is PC via Steam, with Windows 10 minimum and Windows 11 recommended [1]; Team17's game page also lists NVIDIA GeForce NOW [3]. Xbox and PlayStation are planned for "sometime in 2028", with Xbox wishlists open on the Xbox Store (11 Sep 2026) [4][5].

## Editions and pricing (checked 2026-10-08)

| Item | Steam price | Source |
|------|-------------|--------|
| WARDOGS (Standard) | GBP 36.99 | [1] |
| Supporter Edition (base game plus Supporter Pack) | GBP 45.99 | [1] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC, sold separately) | GBP 11.99 | [1] |

The launch press release gave USD 39.99 for Early Access [2], and a pre-launch press piece gave "$39.99 / GBP 36.99" together [7]. These are the same Standard edition in different currencies. GBP 45.99 is the Supporter Edition, a separate SKU. The Supporter Pack is cosmetic only, and there is no other in-game monetisation during Early Access; in-game cash, gold bars and status camouflage are not sold [2]. See economy-foundation for in-game cash. The developers say the game is priced lower during Early Access with a higher price at full release; the full price is not disclosed [1][2].

## Reception (checked 2026-10-08)

Steam shows "Mostly Positive": 79% positive among 63,152 English reviews, plus 143 curator reviews [1]. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026, so the rating label has held through the first four weeks while the volume grew [1][5]. No finer-grained trend data was found.

## Developer roadmap statement

The Steam page lists intended work: more maps, weapons, vehicles and gameplay variety; deeper progression and a stronger seasonal meta game; rewards for combat, support and logistics; new vehicle types including fighter jets; expanded weapon categories and extra objective variants; continued balance, performance and stability work [1]. The launch release adds that work continues toward the wider meta game and long-term systems for the 1.0 release [2]. No dated roadmap to 1.0 is published; the only dated item is Season 02 on 15 Oct 2026 [11].

## Community channels

The Steam store page and Steam News hub for app 1867240 are the primary announcement channel [1][13]. Team17's WARDOGS page links Team17's Discord (discord.com/invite/team17), the Team17 X account and a Team17 YouTube channel [3]. A WARDOGS-specific official Discord or X account was not confirmed; see Open Questions.

| 10 Sep 2026 | Season 1.0 | Church roof exploit fix, report tracking, server browser filtering rework, XP curves for levels 6-50 slowed, many vendor and vehicle price changes | [8] |

## Season 02 (scheduled)

BULKHEAD's "Season 02 Teaser" post of 22 Sep 2026 gave 15 Oct 2026 as the start; no launch time is published (player-reported guess: 16:00 UTC) [11]. Player-reported and unverified: a first progression wipe where cash converts to Gold Bars spendable in a Black Market, plus weather suggested by rain in the teaser [11][12]. Assessment: treat all Season 02 content as unconfirmed until official notes appear; confidence Low.

This reference lists every dated WARDOGS build change found between the August 2026 closed betas and 8 October 2026, with changes grouped by gameplay, economy, servers and bugs. It goes deeper than the one-line patch table in meta-release-foundation and does not restate the release timeline.

Every entry rests on press or community summaries: the Steam News post bodies do not render to automated fetchers, so no official patch note was read directly [1]. The 0.1.2 date resolves to 30 September 2026 (maintenance from 08:00 UTC); one secondary source says "September 29" and is treated as an error [2][3][4][5][6][8]. Season 02 is announced, not live [11].

Confidence is Medium: the change lists agree across independent outlets, but all are secondary, and the hotfix and Season 02 entries are thinner or conflicted.

text:
## Version label conflict

| Label | Date | Used by | Note |
|-------|------|---------|------|
| Season 1.0 | 10 Sep 2026 | Gfinity changelog [10] | Only label given; no build number |
| 0.11 | 14 Sep 2026 | PlayDay [7] | Article states 0.11, not 0.1.1 |
| 0.1.2 | 30 Sep 2026 | Gfinity, MP1st, Bisect, Vice, InGameNews [2][3][4][5][6] | Vice calls it a minor patch, InGameNews substantial [5][6] |

Assessment: 0.11 and 0.1.2 are inconsistent as a numbering scheme (0.11 reads as 0.1.1 in dotted form), so the press probably follows the studio's own inconsistent labels. Confidence Low; no developer explanation was found and no build ID was found.

## 0.1.2 date: 29 vs 30 September

| Claim | Evidence |
|-------|----------|
| 30 Sep 2026, maintenance from 08:00 UTC (01:00 PT), about one hour | MP1st article stamped 30 Sep [3]; Vice, published 30 Sep, same window [5] |
| Deployed 30 Sep | Gfinity, published 30 Sep, "deployed today" [2]; BisectHosting post dated 30 Sep [4]; InGameNews table 30 Sep 06:57 UTC [6] |
| "September 29 patch" | One MMOEXP article, which says its details come from a single podcast [8] |

Assessment: 30 September is correct; 29 September is a secondary-source slip. Confidence High, because five outlets and the maintenance window agree and none of them mentions the 29th.

## Entry index

| Date | Build or label | Official or press | Source |
|------|----------------|-------------------|--------|
| 14 Aug 2026 | Closed beta notes (partial) | Community repost of developer notes, published 21 Aug | [12] |
| 21-23 Aug 2026 | Closed Beta Weekend | Official press release | [13] |
| 3-6 Sep 2026 | Second closed beta | Press | [10] |
| 10 Sep 2026 | Season 1.0 (Early Access launch) | Press | [10] |
| 14 Sep 2026 | 0.11 | Press, full notes | [7] |
| 30 Sep 2026 | 0.1.2 | Press, multiple | [2][3][4][6] |
| 2 Oct 2026 | Security and stability hotfix | Press | [6] |
| 2 Oct 2026 | Balance hotfix | Press, single source | [8][9] |
| 15 Oct 2026 | Season 02 | Announced, not live | [11] |

## Closed beta, notes dated 14 Aug 2026 (partial)

- Gameplay: pistol damage up; AK74, Galil, M4 and FAL handling improved; 122mm damage against air vehicles reduced; Gepard removed from unlock tracks and vendor [12].
- Economy: level-up costs raised above level 15; vehicle and weapon unlock costs raised across classes; sniper kill-streak bonuses removed in No Man's Land; a rebuy bug fixed [12].
- Bugs and UI: held vehicle inputs lost on menu open fixed; Havoc spawning in the shooting range fixed; Hot Zone magnet shrink fixed; HOTAS bindings persist; new Background FPS Limit setting [12].
- The source says the full list was still being compiled [12]. The 21-23 Aug beta weekend is attested by a press release and the 3-6 Sep beta by Gfinity; whether the 14 Aug notes belong to the former is not stated [10][12][13].

## 10 Sep 2026, Early Access launch ("Season 1.0")

- Gameplay: church roof exploit fixed; Z20 Lakota balance pass; helicopter input damping on all devices; vehicle turret rotation cap; 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables take more loadout space; tank aiming DPI fix [10].
- Progression: levels 10-20 slower, curve flattens from level 35; Artillery to Career 90, Heavy Tank to Driver 35. Example bands: level 10 from 25,000 to 35,000 XP; level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000; level 50 from 838,000 to 1,000,000. Air vehicle kill XP 300 to 250 [10].
- Economy: Forward Operating Base vendor price $2,500 to $7,500; Artillery Tank $400,000 to $500,000; Z20 Lakota $50,000 to $35,000; URAL $50,000 to $35,000; supply-crate pricing rescaled to a 1-200 range [10].
- Servers: reworked server browser filtering, community server image scaling fixed, Host button goes to the hosting page, report tracking with weighted reports, ban announcements, voice chat recovery [10].
- Bugs and stability: DLSS Frame Generation toggle without restart, several crash paths fixed, more detailed GPU crash reports [10].

## 14 Sep 2026, Patch 0.11

- Maintenance about one hour from 08:00 UTC [7].
- Servers: browser split into Official and Community; Official lost filters; Community gained text search; Community Server IDs persist across matches and restarts; Show Empty/Full option; more Asia capacity [7].
- Economy: 5% end-of-match cash bonus on Community servers for one week, as an apology; exploit sanctions defined (timed ban plus cash and XP reset; permanent ban for XP-farming servers and for publishing unreported exploit content) [7].
- Bugs: various cash exploits and more GPU crashes fixed [7].
- Gameplay: none completed; community favouriting, priority queues, message of the day, warmup activities, seeding AFK kick disable and team switching were listed as not yet ready [7].

## 30 Sep 2026, Update 0.1.2

- Bugs: WD-L020 crash (Windows 11 KB5124010) fixed; throwables blocked from enclosed vehicle seats; adaptive crosshair hides when aiming; buildable crit spots favour reachable spots; Havoc 20mm and 30mm damage bug fixed; localisation improved [3][4].
- Economy: revive validity checks fully server-side; vehicle fly-through exploit fixed and capped; buildable destruction rewards scale with build progress; FOB pallet deposits outside the zone give reduced reward; cash and progression resets and bans for exploits and real-money trading, with first-time leniency ended [2][3][4].
- Servers: DEPLOY flow (Official, Community, Infantry Mode, Low-Level); Advanced Filters back on Official; full names on hover; queue position; Anonymous mode; gamepad support on DEPLOY [3][4].
- Admin: daily restart time in UTC, RCON AllowedHosts, RCON length caps, Standard response detail default, ServerImageURL checked on load [3][4].

## 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes

- Security and stability hotfix: minor undisclosed issues, no gameplay, balance, economy or UI changes, one-hour maintenance; InGameNews timestamp 00:13 UTC. The same article is ambiguous on whether the maintenance was scheduled or completed [6].
- Balance hotfix: IR rangefinder removed from the vendor until Season 02 and reported to need batteries on return; the anti-air Sea Whiz time to kill a Havoc cut from about 12 s to about 6 s; no download, rolling out as regional servers restart over about 12 hours [8]. This is player-reported podcast material; a search summary of further coverage places this item at 15:39 UTC and one outlet's title links it to a CWIS change [8][9].

## Season 02 (announced, not live)

Announced for 15 Oct 2026 in BULKHEAD's teaser; contents and launch time are not confirmed [11]. Listed only so the sequence is complete; nothing under Season 02 has happened yet.

text:
This is a snapshot taken on 2026-10-08, one week before Season 02, of everything said about Season 02 and the longer Early Access roadmap. It exists so that after launch the real patch notes can be diffed against what was promised and what was rumoured. It deepens meta-release-foundation; it does not repeat its release timeline.

Officially, very little is confirmed. BULKHEAD's Steam post of 22 Sep 2026 gives only the date, 15 October 2026, and a video [1]. The 30 Sep 2026 Update 0.1.2 post describes Season 02 as "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [3], and the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix post says IR Rangefinders return in Season 02 and will need batteries [4]. Two promised "next week" detail posts had not appeared in the Steam News snapshot by 8 Oct 2026 [3][5].

Almost everything else (rain, a progression wipe, cash converting to Gold Bars, new weapons) is press or rumour. Confidence is Low: the core content claims are pre-release and come from press and from commercial sources that sell boosting or in-game cash. A table below grades each rumour so it can be scored after launch.

## Roadmap to 1.0

The roadmap post of 7 Apr 2026 states that the metagame is "our frontend experience that will enable you to continue earning, progressing and adding value to your account even when not in a match" [2]. The post lists two named systems, the Black Market & Vault and the Player Skills & Challenge System, with no season attached [2]. The post's text does not mention seasons, a wipe, or a conversion of cash to Gold Bars; third parties attribute those to the video embedded in it (see the rumour table) [2][15]. No official 1.0 date, Early Access duration or full-release price appears in the Steam posts in the snapshot. A podcast summary on a conflicted site quotes a developer as saying 1.0 is "roughly 23 months out" [17]; see Open Questions.

## Terminology conflict

Official text uses "GOLD MARKET" for the cosmetic store that Gold Bars buy from (18 Feb 2026) [8] and "The Black Market & Vault" for a planned metagame feature (7 Apr 2026) [2]. Dexerto says Gold Bars buy "exclusive cosmetics from the Black Market" [16]. Whether these are one store or two is not resolved by any official source.

text:
This depth document goes below the admin summary in technical-servers-foundation: the RCON HTTP API, the `ServerSettings.ini` keys, the 0.1.2 hardening, the 2 October hotfix, third-party admin tooling and moderation. It is verified against Season 1, patch 0.1.2 plus hotfixes to 2 Oct 2026.

Only two things rest on press or provider secondary sources: the 0.1.2 admin changes (daily restart time in UTC, an `AllowedHosts` RCON setting, capped message lengths, Standard response detail by default, `ServerImageURL` validated at load) [1][2], and the existence and timing of the 2 October hotfix, whose contents were not disclosed [1]. Everything else (port, auth, endpoints, ini keys and defaults, the CL-501228 removals) comes from an unofficial fan reference [3] and a tracker guide written by a tool vendor [4].

Confidence is Low. No official RCON or server-settings document was found, and the main reference was last updated before 0.1.2 shipped.

text:
- The RCON interface is reported to be a versioned HTTP/JSON API (`/v1`), default port 7776, off by default, authenticated by a single shared bearer token with no read-only role (player-reported, reference v0.39 of 2026-09-21) [3][4].
- Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) added an RCON access-restriction setting named AllowedHosts, capped RCON message and broadcast lengths, and made Standard the default response detail [2].
- The fan reference does not mention AllowedHosts at all, because it predates 0.1.2; its key defaults may therefore be stale [3].
- Eight write endpoints were reported removed in build CL-501228 (14 Sep 2026) and replaced by edits to the config document [3].
- The listed `MaxPlayers` default of 128 is unexplained: the game is a 100-player format and no source gives a reason for 128 (see Detail and Open Questions) [3].
- The 2 Oct 2026 hotfix was announced in 26 words with no specifics; any link to RCON is unknown [1].
- Warcon and BattleMetrics are the named third-party panels; Warcon bans work only while the panel runs [4][5].

topic: RCON interface, ServerSettings, admin tooling, security hardening

text:
## Transport and authentication (PR, reference v0.39, 2026-09-21) [3]

| Item | Reported value |
|------|----------------|
| Base URL | `http://<host>:<port>/v1/` |
| Default port | 7776, settable in config or with `-RCONPort=` |
| Transport | Plain HTTP; HTTPS refuses the connection |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>` on every request |
| Roles | One token, full read and write, no read-only key |
| Body format | JSON; the two config-document endpoints use `text/plain` |
| Errors | Non-2xx with `{error:{code,message}}`; 412 stale revision, 422 rejected value, 404 removed route |
| Rate limit | None published |

Conflict: the vendor guide says any listener bound beyond loopback "must use TLS" and that hosts provide an https address [4], while the fan reference says an earlier claim that a network listener needs a certificate was corrected and HTTPS is refused [3]. Both are player-reported. Assessment (confidence Low): terminate TLS in a reverse proxy or use a tunnel rather than expecting the game to do it.

## Endpoints (PR) [3]

| Group | Reported routes |
|-------|-----------------|
| Read | status, players, capabilities, bans, reserved-slots, audit (limit 1-500, default 50), config, rotation, catalog (maps, lightings, experiences, alternators), sponsor, server-id, health |
| Player writes | kick (reason), kill, message, faction change (only if listed in capabilities) |
| Match writes | broadcast, map change, match end, match restart, lighting |
| Bans | POST ban (steamId, optional reason), DELETE ban |
| Config | validate (dry run), PUT replace with `If-Match`, optional `force=true`, `fullApply=true` |

The vendor guide counts "around 35 endpoints" [4]. Clients should read `GET /v1/capabilities` rather than assume a route exists [3].

## Config document semantics (PR) [3]

- `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document; omitted sections are removed.
- Every value is revalidated on each apply; one bad value blocks all edits, and a non-empty `errors` array means nothing was applied.
- Array keys follow Unreal operators: `!Key=ClearArray` empties, `.Key=value` appends.
- Ban, reserve and rotation commands edit and persist back to the ini. Only whitelisted sections and keys are honoured.

## ServerSettings.ini keys (PR; defaults as listed, not verified in-game) [3]

| Section | Key | Listed default | Applies |
|---------|-----|----------------|---------|
| WDRCONSettings | `bEnabled` | listener off by default; the key list shows `true` (inconsistent) | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `BindAddress` | 127.0.0.1 (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `Port` | 7776 | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `Password`, `PasswordHash` | empty password auto-generates to `Saved/RCON/ADMIN-PASSWORD.txt`; hash from `-GenerateRCONHash=` takes precedence | startup |
| WDGameSession | `ServerName` | none | immediately |
| WDGameSession | `ServerPassword` | empty (open) | next restart |
| WDGameSession | `ServerMin/MaxPlayerCash`, `ServerMin/MaxPlayerLevel` | 0 (no limit) | next restart |
| WDGameSession | `ServerImageURL` | none; 1024x256 PNG or JPEG on an allow-list | pending |
| WDGameSession | `MaxReservedSlots` | 20 | immediately |
| WDGameSession | `DefaultReservedPlayerIds`, `DefaultBannedPlayerIds` | one SteamID64 per line | n/a |
| Engine.GameSession | `MaxPlayers` | 128, clamped by a developer-set min and max | immediately |
| PreMatch PlayerCount | `MinimumRequiredPlayers` | 60 | next match |
| KOTH | `ScorePeriod` | 24 s, range 18-30 | next match |
| WDGameStateSession | `bLockOverpopulatedTeamsConfig`, `OverpopulatedTeamThresholdConfig` | true, 2 | next match |
| MapRotationSettings | `bEnabled`, `RotationMode`, `+RotationEntries` | true, Ordered (or Random) | immediately |

The reference states the RCON listener is off by default yet lists `bEnabled` as `true`; this inconsistency is unresolved, so treat the true default as unknown [3].

## MaxPlayers 128 versus a 100-player game

- The game format is 100 players in three teams (Steam page, via the foundation document). A web search of hosting wikis found no source for 128; those pages were not opened and are not relied on.
- The reference says the value is "clamped by a developer-set min and max" [3]. So 128 is at most a stored default, and the effective cap could be lower.
- Assessment (confidence Low): 128 is probably an engine-level or template default, not a supported player count. This is inference. Do not set it above 100 expecting more players, and confirm the clamp with your host.

## Build CL-501228 removals (PR, build dated 2026-09-14) [3]

Removed routes (now 404 on current builds, still served by older builds): `PATCH /v1/settings`, `POST` and `DELETE /v1/reserved-slots`, `POST` and `DELETE /v1/rotation/entries`, `POST /v1/rotation/entries/{i}/move`, `POST /v1/rotation/save`, `PUT /v1/sponsor`. The functions moved to config keys: `DefaultReservedPlayerIds`, `RotationEntries` with `bEnabled` and `RotationMode`, `ScorePeriod`, `ServerImageURL`. The build date coincides with patch 0.11, but no source read ties the two explicitly.

## Hardening in 0.1.2 and the hotfix

| Change | Class | Note |
|--------|-------|------|
| AllowedHosts restricts who can reach RCON | S [1][2] | Value format, wildcard and default are undocumented in every source read |
| Message and broadcast length caps | S [2] | Cap values not published |
| Standard response detail by default | S [2] | Whether Full is still selectable is not documented |
| Config replies stop exposing server internals | S [2] | |
| `ServerImageURL` checked at load | S [2] | Consistent with the reference's allow-list note [3] |
| Server-authoritative revive checks | S [1] | Gameplay exploit fix, not RCON |
| 2 Oct hotfix | S [1] | Contents undisclosed |

## Admin tooling and moderation

- **Warcon** (PR, repository page): self-hosted panel (Bun, SvelteKit, Postgres, Docker Compose), MIT code, with map imagery excluded from the licence and owned by Bulkhead. Per-server roles viewer, operator and admin; stored RCON passwords encrypted (AES-GCM); audit log exportable to CSV or JSON; automation triggers. No game version is stated and commit dates were not visible [5]. The page says the protocol was reverse-engineered, so it can break when builds change [5].
- **Warcon bans** are enforced by the panel's worker, not the game: a banned player is removed when seen, and bans only hold while Warcon runs and reaches the server. Bans made outside the panel appear as "local" [5].
- **BattleMetrics** is reported to support WARDOGS RCON, paid after a free tier, and it stores your RCON password [4]. The vendor guide is by Warcon's publisher, so it is promotional [4].
- **Native bans:** by Steam ID, persisted in the ban list and `DefaultBannedPlayerIds` [3][4].

text:
This depth document extends the technical-servers-foundation with how WARDOGS servers are obtained and found: the hosts-only model, the approved hosts, the Official and Community split introduced in patch 0.11, regions, browser behaviour, slot counts, restart handling and prices. It is verified as far as the sources allow against Season 1, patch 0.1.2 and hotfixes to 2 October 2026. Season 02 is reported for 15 October 2026 and is outside this version [3].

Headline findings: the hosting-count conflict (two versus three) is a dating problem rather than a contradiction. A fan site reporting evidence checked on 1 September 2026 says two unnamed hosts had passed [1]; a guide checked on 13 September says the studio named QONZER and BisectHosting on 7 September and xREALM on 8 September, giving three [3]. Prices, slot sizes and regions are known only from provider pages and fan guides. The 12-hour versus 24-hour restart conflict could not be resolved: no source read states either interval, and the only documented mechanism is a once-daily restart time in UTC [2][3].

Confidence is Low. The patch 0.11 browser facts rest on a press summary of official notes [4], but the approved-host names, prices, slot tiers and regions rest on fan sites and commercial pages, and key claims conflict or are undated.

Statements at Season 1 / patch 0.1.2, checked 2026-10-08.

- **Hosts-only model.** Self-hosting is not supported; the developer is reported to withhold server code, citing security and performance (fan site, evidence dated to 1 Sep 2026; player-reported) [1]. A second guide says no other host has access to the server code [3].
- **Approved hosts.** Three: QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM, named by the studio on 7 and 8 September 2026 according to a fan guide (player-reported, checked 13 Sep 2026) [3]. A tracker (updated 14 Sep 2026) says three approved hosts exist but does not name them [5].
- **Browser.** Community and Official lists since 14 Sep 2026 [4]; the Deploy screen offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level options as of 0.1.2 (player-reported summary) [3].
- **Restart.** Community admins can set a daily restart time in UTC (BisectHosting blog, a provider) [2].
- **Regions.** A tracker lists seven regions it tracks (see Detail) [5]; no official list was found.

text:
## Resolving the host count (2 versus 3)

| Date of evidence | Claim | Source | Class |
|------------------|-------|--------|-------|
| 1 Sep 2026 | Two hosts passed launch standards, names unpublished, more in the pipeline | [1] | Fan site |
| 7 Sep 2026 | Studio names QONZER and BisectHosting (relayed) | [3] | Fan guide |
| 8 Sep 2026 | Studio adds xREALM (relayed) | [3] | Fan guide |
| 14 Sep 2026 | "Only the three approved hosts run WARDOGS servers" | [5] | Tracker |

Assessment: the sequence is consistent with two hosts growing to three in early September; the conflict is stale evidence, not disagreement. Confidence Medium, resting on [1][3][5], all unofficial; the studio posts themselves were not read. Other sellers (XGamingServer, Survival Servers, LOW.MS, Supercraft) advertise WARDOGS hosting but were not on the named list; XGamingServer itself says it is "onboarding" through partners and does not claim approval [7][8]. Treat such pages as pre-approval marketing.

## Official versus Community (patch 0.11, 14 Sep 2026) [4]

| Aspect | Official | Community |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Operator | Bulkhead | Approved host customer |
| Filters | Removed in 0.11 (no modified modes); advanced filters restored in 0.1.2 per foundation | Reliability improved, text search added |
| Quick bar | Show Empty/Full added | Show Empty/Full added |
| Server ID | n/a | Persistent, longer, unique, joinable by ID |
| Naming | Names sorted alphabetically ignoring special characters and numbers; no repeated spaces | Same |

Planned and not shipped per the 0.11 post: favouriting, tiered priority queues, Message of the Day, improved warmup, AFK-kick suspension during seeding, team-switching controls [4]. A one-week 5 percent End of Match cash bonus on Community servers ran from 14 Sep and has ended [3][4].

## Browser behaviour

- Region is picked via Deploy, Server Browser, Region, tick regions, Confirm (player-reported guide) [6]. The 0.1.2 region selector shows how many regions are selected [2].
- Ticking several regions has been reported to return an empty list; guides advise selecting one, and clearing persisted search text (player-reported) [3][6]. A fan site calls the one-region rule a temporary August Beta workaround, not a confirmed Early Access rule [1].
- Asian capacity was increased in 0.11; no slot or per-region figures were published [4].

## Regions

| Source | Regions named | Class |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| Tracker, 14 Sep 2026 | Europe, North America East, North America Central, North America West, Oceania, Asia, South America | Player-reported [5] |
| Guide screenshot caption | Europe, North America, South America, Asia, with ping values | Player-reported [6] |
| Hosting vendor | Datacentres in East/West USA, Europe (Germany), Oceania, Singapore | Commercial [7] |

No official list was found; labels disagree. Oceania as a browser region is unconfirmed [1][6].

## Slots and capacity

Matches are 100 players across three teams per the foundation. Hosts sell by different units: xREALM 60, 80 or 100 player packages; QONZER sells by CPU threads (8, 10 or 12) and says it does not limit slots; the smallest size sold anywhere is 60 slots (player-reported compilation, 13 Sep 2026) [3]. The unofficial config reference lists `MaxPlayers` default 128, "clamped by a developer-set min/max" [9].

## Costs (provider pages as compiled 13 Sep 2026; verify before buying) [3]

| Host | Price shown | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| QONZER | GBP 49.95, 59.95, 69.95 per month | 5% quarterly, 10% semi-annual, 15% annual prepay discounts |
| BisectHosting | from USD 71.99 per month | per-tier prices not visible |
| xREALM | from EUR 59.99 per month | 60/80/100 slots |

Roundups conflict with these figures [3]. Pre-approval pages quote far lower numbers (for example XGamingServer USD 24.50 to 42.00 and a Supercraft reservation page USD 17.99 to 39.99), marked "coming soon" or reservation-only [7][8]; they are not approved-host prices.

## Restart cycles (12 h versus 24 h)

- Documented: a daily restart time, in UTC, settable by community admins since 0.1.2 [2]. This is a once-per-day schedule, which fits "24 h", but no source states a default interval.
- Not documented: the unofficial config reference lists no scheduled-restart key, only on-demand `POST /v1/match/restart`; some session keys apply only at next restart [9].
- The 12 h figure was not found in any source I could open; searches returned only unrelated client memory-leak advice. The foundation's statement that host guides disagree remains unverified. Persistent IDs mean a restart no longer changes a server's identity [4].

## How a prospective admin gets a server

1. Choose one of the three named hosts (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM) [3]. 2. The in-game Host button links to the hosting page [3][4]. 3. Check slots, region, billing term and refund terms on the host's own page [1]. 4. RCON was described in August as in development, with day-one controls limited to maps and modes [1]; RCON additions arrived in 0.1.2 [2] (see rcon-and-server-admin).

text:
This depth document goes beyond the specification table in technical-servers-foundation. It collects what is documented about client performance and stability in WARDOGS (Steam app 1867240): the exact wording and gaps of the Steam requirements, what is and is not stated about upscaling and frame generation, the Linux and Proton position, what a "kernel level" anti-cheat implies for players, the WD-L020 crash and its Windows 11 KB5124010 link, and a patch-by-patch list of performance and crash fixes through the 2 October 2026 hotfix [1][2][3][4][5].

Headline facts: the Steam page lists a 50 GB install, 16 GB RAM and a 1080p Low 60 fps (upscaled) minimum, and does not list DirectX, Steam Deck or Linux [1]. WD-L020 was the main target of update 0.1.2 on 30 September 2026 and was tied by press to Windows 11 update KB5124010 [4][5]. Upscaling settings are confirmed only through a DLSS Frame Generation toggle in launch notes and a player-reported settings guide [2][7].

Confidence is Medium. The specification and anti-cheat line are primary, but patch contents rest on press summaries because Steam news bodies were not readable, and the settings guidance is player-reported.

text:
- The Steam page lists Windows 10 64-bit minimum, Windows 11 64-bit recommended, 16 GB RAM and 50 GB storage for both tiers; no DirectX version, VRAM figure or storage type is given (checked 2026-10-08) [1].
- The minimum is stated as 1080p Low at 60 fps upscaled; the recommended is 1440p Medium 70+ fps native or 4K Medium 60+ fps upscaled, so the minimum assumes an upscaler is on [1].
- The Steam page says "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat" and does not name the product; GamingOnLinux says the studio used Easy Anti-Cheat earlier and appeared to be testing something else (5 Sep 2026) [1][6].
- Linux is unsupported; on 5 Sep 2026 the developers said they cannot commit to Linux for Early Access, that earlier Linux working was accidental, and invited refunds [6]. The Steam page does not mention Steam Deck [1].
- WD-L020 crash fix shipped in update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026), described as the patch's main issue and linked to Windows 11 update KB5124010 [4][5].
- Launch patch (10 Sep 2026) made DLSS Frame Generation switchable without a restart and fixed two frame generation crash paths [2]. Patch 0.11 (14 Sep 2026) added only "more GPU crashes addressed" with no detail [3].
- Player-reported guides rate Global Illumination as the largest single frame-rate cost and recommend installing on an SSD (guide updated 12 Sep 2026) [7].

text:
## Specification wording (Steam, 2026-10-08) [1]

| Item | Minimum | Recommended |
|------|---------|-------------|
| OS | Windows 10, 64-bit | Windows 11, 64-bit |
| CPU | Intel Core i5 8600 or AMD Ryzen 5 3500 | Intel Core i7 12700K or AMD Ryzen 7 5700X |
| RAM | 16 GB | 16 GB |
| GPU | Nvidia GTX 1660 or AMD Radeon RX 590 | Nvidia RTX 3070 or AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT |

| Note | 1080p Low, 60 fps (upscaled) | 1440p Medium 70+ fps (native), or 4K Medium 60+ fps (upscaled) |
| DirectX | Not listed | Not listed |

Gaps in the official figures: no VRAM, no storage type (SSD or HDD), no Windows 11 requirement for the minimum tier, and no DirectX or Vulkan statement [1]. The minimum tier mixes a 2018-era GTX 1660 class GPU with an "upscaled" target, so players below it should expect to rely on an upscaler. Assessment: that reading is an inference from the note wording, Confidence Medium, resting on [1].

## Graphics and upscaling settings

- **Documented officially:** DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without restarting the game and the render target pool is configurable (10 Sep 2026 launch changelog, press summary) [2]. Shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores instead of being disabled, and shadow cache refreshes were reduced to cut hitching when taking control of a character [2].
- **Not documented in the sources read:** an FSR or XeSS option list, DLSS quality modes, or a Reflex entry. The launch changelog does not mention FSR, general upscaling options or memory changes [2].
- **Player-reported settings guide** (allthings.how, "Updated Sep 12, 2026"): lists an Overall Quality Custom profile; Global Illumination as the biggest single gain at roughly 20 percent on average; Shadows, Reflections, Shading, Post-Processing and Particle Spawn Rate at Low; Texture Streaming reduced first on VRAM warnings; DLSS on RTX cards and FSR on others, with Quality as the usual balance; Nvidia Reflex and a frame limit matching refresh rate [7]. These are one site's recommendations, not developer guidance, and the figure is not independently measured.
- A search of other community guides found disagreement on Global Illumination (off versus kept on with lower Shadows) and on DLSS Performance versus Quality mode; that search summary is not cited as fact. Treat all settings advice as player-reported.

## Linux, Steam Deck and Proton

| Date | Statement | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 5 Sep 2026 | Developers "cannot commit to having Linux support for our Early Access launch"; still working on Proton compatibility; stance unchanged since before release | [6] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | An earlier community-manager Discord post implying support was called a communication mistake; earlier Linux functionality in alpha and beta tests was accidental | [6] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | Buyers who expected Proton support on 10 Sep were told to refund | [6] |
| 25 Sep 2026 | A reader comment on the article quotes the developers as having no new information and still wanting Linux support via Proton (player-reported, unverified) | [6] |

Steam Deck: the Steam page and GamingOnLinux article give no Steam Deck status [1][6]. No Deck Verified rating was found; treat Deck as unsupported and untested.

## Kernel-level anti-cheat and what it implies

- Fact: the Steam page states the game "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat" [1]. GamingOnLinux says the game previously used Easy Anti-Cheat, the developers appear to be testing something else, and the product is not named; the site said it would check at release [6]. This document does not name the product. A reader comment on that article names one, which is unverified and not repeated here.
- Assessment: a kernel driver generally installs at game launch, needs administrator rights, and limits some virtualization and driver-level tools; kernel anti-cheat also commonly conflicts with Linux compatibility layers unless the vendor enables Proton support. Confidence Low to Medium: this is general reasoning, not a WARDOGS-specific statement, and the sources above do not confirm the mechanism for this game.
- Player-reported: a reader comment says the beta ran on Windows only with the new anti-cheat and had many cheaters, and that Linux ran better in the previous beta [6]. Anecdotal.
- Moderation side (not kernel-specific): a report-weighting system and ban announcements were added at launch [2]; see technical-servers-foundation.

## WD-L020 and KB5124010

- Update 0.1.2 on 30 Sep 2026 lists a "Windows 11 'WD-L020' Crash Error Fix"; MP1st calls it "the main issue tackled by this patch" and says the update KB5124010 caused the recent WD-L020 crashes [5].
- In-Game News independently reports the WD-L020 fix and links it to KB5124010, and says the notes contain no other GPU, DLSS or FSR items [4].
- No source read describes the mechanism, which hardware was affected, or a pre-patch workaround. Uninstalling the Windows update is not recommended by any source; do not infer it.

text:
This document covers what a player or server admin needs technically for WARDOGS (Bulkhead / Team17, Steam app 1867240) in Early Access: official system requirements, anti-cheat, platform support, the Community and Official server browsers, how community servers are hosted, the admin and RCON tooling, and modding status. It is verified against the Steam store page and press summaries of patch notes up to Season 1, patch 0.1.2 (30 September 2026) and the security hotfix of 2 October 2026 [1][6].

Headline facts: the Steam page lists a Windows 10/11 64-bit requirement, kernel-level anti-cheat, and no mention of dedicated servers or mods [1]. Patch 0.11 (14 September 2026) split the browser into Community and Official lists [3]. Community servers are reportedly rented from Bulkhead-approved hosts; the only statements on this are relayed through a fan site and a tracker guide, not read first-hand from Bulkhead [9][11]. No official RCON documentation was found; the detailed admin reference is an unofficial fan document [10].

Confidence is Medium. Steam page facts are primary, but patch contents rest on press summaries because Steam news bodies do not render to fetchers, and the whole hosting and admin layer rests on unofficial or provider material.

## System requirements (Steam page, 2026-10-08)

Source for the table: [1].

## Performance and settings changes at launch (Season 1 changelog, 10 Sep 2026) [4]

- DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without a restart; the render target pool is configurable.
- Shadow cache refreshes were reduced (less hitching when taking control of a character); shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores instead of being disabled.
- Dropped items no longer affect navigation.
- Startup reliability improved with clearer early-failure messages and a recovery path; a legacy graphics dependency was removed.
- Crash fixes covered two frame generation paths, network calls scheduled off the game thread, a chatbox tooltip, buildables, and firing a weapon whose owner had left. GPU crash reports include more detail.
- Voice chat recovery after a failed join and under load was improved.
- Netcode: none of the sources read describe tick rate, prediction or lag compensation. This is a gap, not a finding.

## Moderation and anti-cheat systems

- A report tracking system weights reports so repeat and bad-faith reporters have less influence; cheater bans are announced in the server when match termination is off; the "kicked from server" message appears only for real bans [4].
- Patch 0.11 states cash exploits get a timed ban plus a reset of cash and XP; exploit tutorials count as advertising cheats and risk permanent bans; the developer states "We track every server you enter" and joining known XP farming servers for more than a few minutes risks a permanent ban [3].

## Server browser timeline

| Date | Change |
|------|--------|
| 10 Sep 2026 | Filtering reworked; Host button links to the hosting page; community image scaling fixed [4] |
| 14 Sep 2026 (0.11) | Community and Official browsers; text search and Show Empty/Full toggle for Community; persistent longer server IDs; Asian capacity increased; 5% End of Match cash bonus on Community servers for one week [3] |
| 30 Sep 2026 (0.1.2) | New Deploy flow pointing to Infantry Mode and Low-Level community servers; advanced filters restored to the Official list [6] |

Planned but not shipped per the 0.11 post: favouriting, tiered priority queues, Message of the Day, improved warmup, no AFK kicks during seeding, team switching controls [3].

text:
Source warning: no official server-admin manual from Bulkhead was found. Everything in this section other than the 0.1.2 admin changes comes from unofficial or provider material and is labelled.

**Hosting model.**

- A fan site (self-described as unofficial, checked 2026-09-01) relays an official thread saying server code will not be released for everyone to host, citing performance and security, and that individuals rent from approved hosts [9]. Player-reported.
- A server-tracking site says there is no official developer documentation, that only three approved hosts run servers, and that RCON access depends on the host's panel [11]. Player-reported.
- Consequence for admins: you probably cannot run your own SteamCMD or Docker server; confirm with your host. Several commercial hosting pages advertised pre-launch capacity; treat these as marketing, not evidence of an available server download.

**Admin changes confirmed in 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026)** [5][6][7]:

- Daily scheduled restart time, set in UTC.
- RCON AllowedHosts setting to restrict which hosts can reach RCON.
- RCON message and broadcast lengths capped; RCON responses default to Standard detail rather than Full; config responses no longer expose server internals.
- ServerImageURL is validated at config load.
- Since 0.11, community server IDs persist across map changes and restarts [3].

**Unofficial RCON and config reference** (fan site, self-described as not official docs and subject to change; player-reported) [10]:

- RCON is plain HTTP REST with JSON, base `http://<host>:<port>/v1/`, default port 7776 (`-RCONPort=`), no TLS, so the password crosses the network in clear text.
- Authentication is `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>`; one token has full read and write access; there is no read-only role. The listener is off by default (`bEnabled` in `[/Script/WDRCON.WDRCONSettings]`).
- Endpoint groups: status, players, bans, config, rotation, capabilities; writes include kick, kill, message, ban, broadcast and match map/end/restart. `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document and supports `If-Match` revision checks.
- Listed `ServerSettings.ini` keys include `ServerName`, `ServerPassword`, `ServerImageURL` (1024x256), cash and level min/max limits, `MaxReservedSlots` (default 20), `MaxPlayers` (listed default 128), `MinimumRequiredPlayers` (default 60), KOTH `ScorePeriod` (default 24 s) and map rotation (`Ordered` or `Random`).
- Several endpoints were reported removed in build ++Wardogs+Live-CL-501228 (2026-09-14) in favour of the config document [10].
- Assessment: because RCON uses one shared secret over unencrypted HTTP, restrict AllowedHosts and keep it on a private network or behind a TLS proxy. Confidence Medium, resting on [6] and [10].

**Third-party tools** (player-reported, not endorsed): Warcon, an open-source (MIT) self-hostable multi-server RCON panel with per-admin roles and audit log [13]; BattleMetrics has reportedly added WARDOGS RCON support [11]. The guide at [11] was written by Warcon's builders, so its recommendations are promotional.

**Hosting provider material** (secondary): BisectHosting summarises the 0.1.2 admin changes [5]; its support article on changing the automatic restart time returned HTTP 403 and is not cited. Host guides disagree on any built-in restart timer value (12 h versus 24 h of uptime); unverified.

**Modding.** The Steam page lists no mod support [1]. No official modding toolkit or plan was found.

**Client notes.** Kernel-level anti-cheat is listed [1]; Linux is unsupported [8]; Windows 11 update KB5124010 caused crash WD-L020, fixed 30 Sep 2026 [6].

text:
This document goes deeper than the parent foundation on WARDOGS aircraft (all helicopters in Early Access) and the systems that counter them. The Steam page lists helicopters in Early Access and fighter jets only for the full release [1]. Official Steam posts name only a few air facts: the Havoc, the Z20 Lakota, flare deployables, a vehicle fly-through reward cap, a Havoc cannon-damage bug fix, and a 2 Oct 2026 hotfix that disabled IR Rangefinders in the vendor and cut the time for the CIWS to destroy a Havoc from about 12 s to about 6 s [2][3][4].

The official 2 Oct balance post settles a press conflict: there were two separate hotfixes that day, a no-gameplay security and stability hotfix and, later, a balance hotfix [3][5]. The official post says "IR Rangefinders" (its title says "IR Goggles") [3].

The roster, prices and Pilot levels come only from player-reported guides, which conflict, so confidence is Medium. All values are a baseline before the Season 02 wipe due 15 Oct 2026 [6].

text:
- Fighter jets are planned for full release only; Early Access air vehicles are helicopters (Steam page, 2026-10-08) [1].

text:
This document goes deeper than the parent foundation on forward operating bases (FOBs), the three hammer tiers, supply types, buildable structures and pallet logistics. It is a pre-Season-02 baseline: Season 02 is due 15 October 2026 and is expected to wipe progression, so every number is tabulated with its version and source class for mechanical diffing later.

The official Steam posts (saved locally and cited by Steam URL) settle the two conflicts the foundation left open. Large Hammer unlock moved from Support level 7 to level 8 in the Season 1 changelog, so level 8 is the current official value [1]. The Support-track Large Hammer unlock rose from $25,000 to $75,000 and the Medium Hammer unlock from $10,000 to $25,000 [1]. No source retrieved gives an $800 hammer price; see Open Questions. The FOB vendor price is $7,500 [1].

Confidence is Medium. Prices, levels and the 0.1.2 reward rules are official [1][2], but the build procedure, structure list, supply types and structure costs rest on player-reported guides [8][9][10], and no official text lists them.

text:
## Baseline values

Source class: Official = Steam announcement posts; Player = player-reported guide, not independently verified. "Season 1.0" is the 9 Sep 2026 changelog.

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| FOB vendor price $7,500 (was $2,500) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Large Hammer vendor price $2,400 (was $1,600) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Support: Medium Hammer unlock $25,000 (was $10,000) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Support: Large Hammer unlock $75,000 (was $25,000) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Support: Large Hammer unlock level 8 (was 7) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Medium Hammer unlock level 3 | Season 1 era | Player [8][9] |
| Small Hammer default, $100 | Season 1 era | Player [8][9] |
| Build Supplies $10 each, $500 per 50 | Season 1 era | Player [8] |
| Pilot: small armoured supply crate $10,000 (was $5,000) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Driver: Large Supply Crate unlock level 16 (was 20) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Driver: Kodiak Flatbed $35,000 (was $15,000), level 10 (was 2) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Supply crate purchase curve rescaled to 1-200 (was 25-250) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Supply crate item sold under $75: 1 XP (was 25 XP) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Buildable destruction reward scales with build progress (no figure published) | 0.1.2 | Official [2] |
| Pallet deposit outside FOB zone: reduced reward (no figure published) | 0.1.2 | Official [2] |
| Supply costs: Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901, Drill Rig 1,351 | Season 1 era | Player [9] |
| CIWS kill time on Havoc about 6 seconds (was 12) | 2 Oct hotfix | Official [5] |

## FOB price and mechanics

The vendor price is the only officially published FOB number; the raise was made so the FOB and Large Hammer are "more of a choice" [1]. Official posts describe the FOB as a way to fortify a chokepoint and list building as an Early Access feature [3][4]. Player-reported procedure: deploy the kit on valid ground, not inside a building, a main base or another FOB's radius; deposit supplies into base storage through the FOB console; choose a structure from the build wheel; finish it with the hammer [8]. FOBs do not refill by themselves [9]. Enemies reaching the FOB console can reportedly hack the base, with a siren [8]. FOB count limits, radius and health are not published.

## The four supply types

All four are player-reported [8]; no official post names them.

| Supply type | Used by (player-reported) |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| Build | Structures; $10 each or $500 per 50 [8] |
| Ammo | Mortar, CIWS, SAM [8] |
| Fuel | Refuel Station, Drill Rig [8] |
| Mechanical | Repair Station [8] |

Official text confirms only supply crates as a purchasable item class (Pilot small armoured supply crate, Driver Large Supply Crate, Kodiak Flatbed) [1] and that helicopters can ferry supplies to teammates [4].

## Hammer tiers and unlocks

| Tier | Unlock | Structures needing the tier (player-reported) |
|------|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Small | Default; $100 (player-reported) [8][9] | Sandbags, barbed wire, hedgehogs, Recon Tent; no FOB needed [8] |
| Medium | Support track, $25,000 (official) [1]; level 3 (player-reported) [8][9] | HESCO, doors, gates [8] |
| Large | Support track, level 8, $75,000 (official) [1]; vendor $2,400 (official) [1] | Bunkers, Recon Towers, mortars, anti-air, Repair and Refuel Stations, Drill Rig [8] |

The required tier reportedly applies only to starting a blueprint; any hammer finishes it [8]. Hammers switch to Dismantle on finished objects and also repair [9].

Conflict resolution:

- **Level 7 versus 8.** The Season 1 changelog states "Large Hammer: level 7 to level 8" [1]. One guide still gave level 7 [9]; that is the pre-Season-1 value. Level 8 is the baseline.
- **$800 versus $25,000.** The official changelog gives $25,000 as the Medium Hammer Support unlock (previously $10,000) and as the former Large Hammer unlock, now $75,000 [1]. No retrieved official or press text gives an $800 hammer price. Any $800 figure is unsupported here; see Open Questions.
- **Vendor versus unlock.** The Support track gates the right to buy the hammer ($75,000, level 8), and the vendor charges $2,400 for a Large Hammer [1]. Whether the vendor price recurs per purchase is not stated.

## Buildable structures and costs

No official structure list or cost table exists in the posts retrieved. Player-reported supply costs [9]: Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901, Drill Rig 1,351. Repair Stations repair and Refuel Stations refuel vehicles from stored supplies; the Drill Rig is reported to pull the Hot Zone toward a fuelled FOB [10]. Gates admit vehicles, doors are infantry-only, hedgehogs block vehicle routes [9]. Official: the CIWS was rebalanced on 2 Oct 2026 [5].

## Pallet delivery and the 0.1.2 reward reduction

Pallets are the logistics unit for moving supplies into a FOB; cargo vehicles carry small amounts and larger loads move on pallets (player-reported) [9]. Update 0.1.2 states: "Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone now awards reduced rewards" [2]. A press summary lists the same change among the cash and XP exploit fixes [7]. The size of the reduction and the zone boundary are not published. The post frames the change as anti-exploit and warns that players abusing repeatable exploits risk a permanent ban [2]. Supply crate sale XP was cut separately in Season 1 [1].

## Build-destroy interaction

Official: "Any rewards for destroying buildables now scale with their build progress - so destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward" [2]. Rocket launchers can take down apartment blocks per the store page [4]. Player-reported: anything built can be destroyed, artillery can level fortifications from outside the zone, and unprotected pallets can be destroyed [8][9]. For diffing: reward scaling is by build progress, with no published curve.

text:
This is a pre-Season-02 baseline of every vehicle named in official WARDOGS text. The only official vehicle prices and unlock levels are in the Season 1 changelog posted on Steam on 9 Sep 2026 [1]. It names about a dozen vehicle entries and lists only the values it changed. It gives no complete roster, no crew sizes and no spawn prices. Everything else (spawn prices, the Gepard, the L2A6, the Havoc's price, the Lakota's level) is guide-only [5][6].

Where official text and the guides disagree, the official text wins and the conflict is recorded. The main findings: the guides' "Kodiak (pickup)" matches the official Kodiak Flatbed (Driver 10, $35,000 after the 10 Sep change) [1]. The official Lakota price is $35,000 but no official Lakota level exists, so the guides' Pilot 10 and Pilot 25 stay unresolved [1][5][6]. The Gepard and L2A6 do not appear in any official post retrieved.

Document confidence is Medium: the numbers that exist are official, but the roster is incomplete and the spawn-price column is player-reported only. Season 02 (due 15 Oct 2026) is expected to change these values.

text:
WARDOGS pairs a combined-arms vehicle set (tanks, an artillery tank, helicopters, light ground vehicles) with player-built Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) and a destructible battlefield. The Steam page confirms that vehicles and logistics are part of Early Access, that players can build a forward operating base to fortify a chokepoint, that rocket launchers can take down apartment blocks, and that fighter jets are planned only for the full release [1].

Official sources give no vehicle table. Names, prices and unlock levels here come from the Season 1 launch changelog as reproduced by press [2] and from community guides, which are labelled player-reported and disagree in places. Build and logistics mechanics (hammer tiers, supply types, pallets) are likewise guide-sourced [5][6][7]. Update 0.1.2 changes to rewards for destroying buildables and delivering pallets are confirmed by two press summaries [3][4].

Document confidence is Medium: the headline mechanics are official, but nearly every number rests on press reproductions or player reports, and Early Access churns per patch.
